questions.question: Differentiate between free range and cage methods in chicken farming. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate between free range and cage methods in chicken farming [U]/[CO1)
  • Free range system is an old and conventional method. The birds are allowed to roam in the open area
  • without fencing. The feeding and breeding of the birds are not taken care of. In this system, investment is nil
  • and large number of birds are lost by predation. This method is often used for indigenous breeds.
  • Cage System or Battery System is a modern method in which individual birds are kept in cages which are
  • arranged in rows and tires one above the other. Feeders and waterers must be provided outside the cage. The
  • initial investment and the cost of replacement of the cages are comparatively high. This system is commonly
  • used for layers to fac ilitate egg collection and maintenance of hygiene.The advantages of this system are
  • low space requirement, prevent cannibalism, assessment of individual performance, easy identification of
  • infectious birds and culling (Any 3 differences- 3 marks)

questions.question: Comment on the causative organism, symptoms and control measures of Foot and Mouth Disease. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Comment on the causative organism, symptoms and control measures of Foot and Mouth Disease
  • [U]/[CO1]
  • Causative organism- Foot and Mouth Disease virus
  • Symptoms- high fever, followed by the appearance of vesicles (blisters) in the mouth, on the tongue, gums,
  • lips, teats and between the hooves. These blisters rupture, leading to excessive salivation, lameness,
  • difficulty in eating and walking,weight loss and a significant drop in milk yield and productivity.
  • Control of FMD mainly on regular vaccination, strict quarantine measures and movement control of animals
  • during outbreaks. Sanitation, disinfection of premises and isolation of infected animals. (3 Points- 3 marks)

questions.question: Comment on algal blooms and the methods of their control. / [CO1, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Comment on algal blooms and the methods of their control [U]/[ CO3]
  • Algal blooms are sudden outbursts of algal forms in association with heavy doses of inorganic fertilizers like
  • urea and super phosphate. They are the result of multiplication of unicellular and filamentous algae. Algal
  • blooms are temporary or permanent. Permanent blooms may cause a surface scum, which in turn may lead to
  • fish mortality. (3 Points- 1.5 marks)
  • Control of Algal blooms:
  •  Copper sulphate 1 ppm/ha packed in cloth bags and immersed in ponds is known to eradicate algal
  • blooms.
  •  Introducing the duckweed, Lemna which forms a shade over the algae and prevents their growth.
  •  Viruses which prevent photo assimilation of carbon dioxide can also be used.
  •  Introduction of algal feeding fishes like Silver carp.(3 Points- 1.5 marks)

questions.question: What is artificial insemination? Comment on their advantages. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• What is artificial insemination? Comment on their advantages [U]/[CO1]
  • Artificial insemination is a reproductive technology used in animal breeding in which semen from a superior
  • quality bull is collected, processed, stored in liquid nitrogen and artificially introduced into the reproductive
  • tract of a female cow during estrus to achieve fertilization.
  • Advantages
  • • Artificial insemination allows the use of semen from genetically superior bulls resulting in better quality
  • offspring and improvement in the genetic features of the cattle herd.
  • • This method also helps to overcome challenges posed by geographical distances or lack of suitable
  • breeding males in remote rural areas. Semen of exotic breeds can be collected and transported to inseminate
  • indigenous breeds promoting cross breeding.
  • • The semen obtained from a single ejaculate can be used to fertilize many cows and the semen of any breed
  • can be introduced into the cow for conception
  • • Artificial insemination ensures better planning and synchronization of breeding activities.
  • • Even old and injured sires can be used for collecting semen. Storage of sperms is possible for many years
  • and the sperms of desirable traits are available for many years even after the bull has died.
  • • Farmers can breed their cows with the best available bulls without maintaining a male on the farm, saving
  • the cost and botherations involved in maintaining bulls.
  • • This method is followed under strict hygiene and good sanitary conditions, reduces the risks associated
  • with natural breeding, including the spread of sexually transmitted diseases and injuries to animals .
  • (Definition-1 mark; Any 4 advantages-4 marks)

questions.question: Discuss the characteristics and compatibility of Khaki Campbell and Indian Runner ducks as layer breeds. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the characteristics and compatibility of Khaki Campbell and Indian Runner ducks as layer
  • breeds [U]/[CO1]
  • Khaki Campbell is the most popular exotic breed in India and globally, rea red for egg production.
  • Originating in England, it is known for its remarkable prolific egg-laying ability, producing around 300–320
  • eggs per year. The name ‘Khaki’ refers to the fawn or light brown color of its plumage, which resembles
  • military khaki uniforms. Khaki Campbell ducks are small to medium -sized, a straight neck and an upright
  • stance. It weighs around 1.6 to 2.2 kg and is known for its early maturity. The eggs are white to pale green in
  • color and are rich in nutrients. These ducks are hardy and adapt well to various climates, including the
  • tropical conditions of India. They are non -broody, meaning they rarely sit on their eggs, which allows for
  • continuous egg production. They are also good foragers and thrive in semi-intensive and extensive systems,
  • feeding on insects, snails and weeds. Due to their calm nature and high egg yield, they are ideal for both
  • small-scale rural farmers and commercial duck farms.
  • Indian Runner is a unique and highly productive indigenous duck breed of India, well -known for its egg-
  • laying capacity. Indian Runners have distinctive upright posture stand tall like a penguin and run rather than
  • waddle, so they got their name. This breed originated in the Indian subcontinent Indian Runner ducks are
  • lightweight, slender, and h ave long necks and legs. They come in various colors such as white, fawn and
  • black. These ducks are excellent layers, producing around 250 to 300 eggs annually and are considered one
  • of the best indigenous layer duck breeds.They are particularly suited for low-input, free-range and wetland
  • farming systems due to their excellent foraging abilities. Indian Runners feed on insects, snails and leftover
  • grains, making them cost-effective to raise. Due to their adaptability, disease resistance and high egg output,
  • Indian Runners are an ideal choice for integrated farming systems and rural backyard poultry, especially in

questions.question: Outline the preventive measures for dysentery. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Outline the preventive measures for dysentery [U]/[C02]
  • Preventive measures include maintaining good personal hygiene, using clean drinking water and ensuring
  • proper sanitation. These are several ways to prevent these illnesses
  • • Wash hands before and after preparing food or eating.
  • • High standards of personal hygiene as well as local hygiene including sanitation must be practiced in order
  • to prevent the disease from spreading.
  • • Flush or discard any stool in the toilet and clean surrounding area using hot water and detergent.
  • • Wash hands thoroughly after using the toilet, changing a diaper or cleaning up a child who has used the
  • toilet, before and after attending to someone who is ill with diarrhoea.
  • • Wash hands after handling animals, contact with animal quarters, cleaning up animal faeces or gardening.
  • • Drink properly treated water. Do not swallow water while swimming in swimming pools, hot tubs or any
  • other water bodies. (Any 5 Points - 5 marks)

questions.question: What are the nutritional and economic importance of poultry eggs? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What are the nutritional and economic importance of poultry eggs? [K]/[CO1]
  • Nutritional Importance:
  • • Chicken eggs are often called a ‘complete food’ because they contain almost all essential nutrients required
  • by the body.
  • • Chicken egg provides around 6–7 grams of protein, containing all nine essential amino acids.
  • • It is rich in vitamins such as A, D, E, B2 (riboflavin), B6, B12, and minerals like iron, phosphorus,calcium,
  • selenium and zinc.
  • • The yolk also contains healthy fats, including omega-3 fatty acids and choline, which is important for brain
  • development and liver function.
  • • They are affordable and easily digestible, making them ideal for all age groups including children, pregnant
  • women and the elderly.
  • • Regular egg consumption helps to reduce malnutrition and protein deficiency in developing countries like
  • India. (Any 5 Points - 0.5 marks each)
  • Economic Importance:
  • • Egg production provides a steady source of income for farmers, especially small house holds and women in
  • rural areas.
  • • Inedible eggs and shells are used in the preparation of animal foods as mineral mixtures and fertilizers
  • • Fertile eggs are used for hatching and for the preparation of vaccines.
  • • Egg white is used in the manufacture of pharmaceuticals, paints, varnishes, adhesives and printing ink. It is
  • also used in book binding,clarification of wine, tanning leather, textile dyeing and in photography.
  • • Egg yolk is used in the manufacture of soaps, paints and shampoos.
  • • Surplus egg production contributes to national food security and export potential. (Any 5 Points - 0.5
  • marks each)

questions.question: What is composite fish culture? Name three species commonly reared in composite fish culture and mention how their distinct ecological niches reduce competition. / [CO3] [5x4 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• What is composite fish culture? Name three species commonly reared in composite fish culture and
  • mention how their distinct scological niches reduce competition [U]/[CO3]
  • Fish culture in which compatible and non-competing fishes are cultured simultaneously by utilizing different
  • feeding zones of a water body so as to increase the total production from unit area is known as composite
  • fish culture. It is also known as polyculture or mixed farming.
  • The best combination in India in a polycultur e system is Rohu, Catla, Mrigal. Catla is a surface feeder and
  • feeds on only Zooplankton.Rohu is a column feeder and utilizes the plankton of that area only. Mrigal is
  • bottom feeder and feed on the plankton which is available at the bottom, mostly benthos.
  • OR Common carp, Silver carp and Grass carp. Common carp is bottom feeder, eats the detritus only. Silver
  • carp is a surface feeder, but feeds only on phytoplankton. Grass carp feed only on aquatic vegetation.)
  • Fishes with complementary feeding habits helps to utilize efficiently the natural food present at diff erent
  • ecological niches in the pond for maximum fish production. The fishes never face any competition for space
  • and food and grow well.
  • (Definition-1.5 marks; name of 3 species-1.5 marks; explanation -2marks)
  • [5x4=20]
